seoTitle: Free RLP Encoder and Decoder for Ethereum
metaDescription: Encode JSON into Ethereum RLP hex, or decode RLP hex into nested values, with checks for non-canonical encodings. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Switch between encode and decode. In encode mode, give a JSON value and get RLP hex; in decode mode, paste RLP hex and get nested hex strings back.
why: Recursive Length Prefix is the serialisation format Ethereum uses for transactions, blocks and trie nodes, and it is also the first step in working out a CREATE contract address. Reading a raw transaction by eye is hopeless, since the length prefixes are mixed in with the data. This tool lets you build RLP from a JSON structure, where strings beginning 0x are raw bytes, other strings are UTF-8 text, numbers are non-negative integers and arrays are lists, or take apart a hex blob into nested items. The decoder rejects non-canonical forms, such as leading zeros in lengths or single bytes wrapped when they need not be, and trailing data after the item. All of it runs in your browser.
howTo: Enter JSON such as ["cat", "dog", 1024] to encode, or RLP hex to decode.
Read the hex output or the nested JSON, and copy it.

faq.q: How are JSON values mapped to bytes when encoding?
faq.a: Strings starting with 0x become raw bytes, other strings become UTF-8 bytes, numbers become the shortest big-endian integer, and arrays become RLP lists. Zero encodes as an empty byte string.

faq.q: Why can't I encode a large number?
faq.a: JSON numbers must be non-negative safe integers. For bigger values, write them as a hex string such as 0x0de0b6b3a7640000, which is treated as bytes.

faq.q: What does the decoder do with invalid input?
faq.a: It reports the first problem: truncated data, lengths larger than the input, non-canonical lengths or trailing bytes. Strict checks help catch malformed transactions.

faq.q: Does decoding show text or numbers?
faq.a: No. Every item comes back as a hex string, since RLP itself carries no type information. You decide whether bytes mean a number, an address or text.
